layout_dets.html:
AdditiveFunctionApplicable materialsProminent examples
BinderIncrease mechanical strength upon hardening of technical bodyInorganic oxide with refractory propertiesAlumina, aluminium phosphate, silica, silica-alumina, natural clays (attapulgite, bentonite, kaolin, montmorillonite, sepiolite) titania, zirconia
FillerDilute active phase to optimise content in technical bodyLow cost inorganic oxide with refractory propertiesNatural clays (e.g. kaolin), alumina
LubricantReduce friction during mixing and shaping operationsOil or other viscous liquidEthylene glycol, glycerin, graphite, mineral oil, propylene glycol, aluminium stearate
ModifierEnhance performance of a technical catalystPromoter, selective poison, co-catalyst, coke or metal traps, passivatorsMetal or metal oxide precursor, clay, zeolite
PeptiserDisperse particles to improve feed homogeneity prior to/during shapingCommonly a mineral or organic acid, but can also be a baseAcetic, citric, formic, hydrochloric, nitric or sulphuric, phosphoric acid
PlasticiserDecrease viscosity of pre- mixtures to facilitate processingMaterial dependent; typically containing polar and non-polar functionalityHydroxyethyl cellulose, polyethylene glycol, starch, sugars, water
PorogenIncrease interparticle porosity in technical bodyCheap material which is removed, typically by thermal decomposition during hardeningCarbon black, flax, sawdust, starches of different size (corn, rice, potato)
